title: NCEP R1 and R2 ocean surface temperature fell 0.32-0.37 C in steps after 11 February 2020 (60S-60N); with a 2020 snow error this makes R1 2020-2026 global 2 m temperature 0.2-0.27 C too cold
abstract: Question: do the SST input changes that put steps into DOISST and OI SST v2 also put steps into atmospheric reanalyses? Approach: we put the ocean skin temperature of NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1 (R1), NCEP-DOE Reanalysis 2 (R2) and CFSR/CFSv2 on one T62 grid and compared it with COBE-SST2, ERSSTv5 and DOISST v2.1 over ice-free ocean, 1982-2026. We fitted steps with autocorrelation-robust errors and measured the effect on 2 m temperature (T2m) against ERA5, NOAAGlobalTemp v6 and GHCN-CAMS. Results: R1 and R2 followed OI SST v2 until 2019. Then their 60S-60N skin temperature fell in three steps: on 11-12 February 2020 (-0.11 to -0.23 C, a one-day step), in December 2022 when NOAA stopped the weekly 1-degree OISST (-0.13 to -0.17 C), and in July 2023 (-0.03 to -0.06 C). The total is -0.32 to -0.37 C against in situ-based products. The ocean still follows ENSO, with an offset. About 45% of the step reaches R1 ocean T2m. R1 snow cover also broke in 2020: summer snow-covered land north of 30N doubled, and R1 summer land T2m is 2-3 C too cold over northern Asia. R1 global T2m is 0.22 C (2020-2022) and 0.27 C (2023-2026) colder than ERA5, and R1 keeps 2016 as its warmest year. With fitted steps removed, 2024 is warmest. CFSR follows DOISST and keeps its 2005 step; CFSv2 has smaller December 2022 and July 2023 SST steps (total -0.11 to -0.20 C) with little effect on its global T2m. Limitations: the causes of the 2020 and 2023 changes are not documented; dates and patterns are the only attribution; references have their own small steps.

display.caption: Ocean skin temperature of NCEP R1 (with R2 dotted) and CFSR/CFSv2 minus three SST products, ice-free ocean 60S-60N, 2014-2019 mean set to zero. R1 and R2 fall by about 0.35 C in steps on 11 February 2020, in December 2022 and in July 2023. CFSv2 has smaller steps in December 2022 and July 2023. Bottom: daily R1 minus ERA5 and minus DOISST, showing the one-day step on 11-12 February 2020.

Left: annual global 2 m temperature anomalies (1991-2020 base). R1 and R2 stay below ERA5 and NOAAGlobalTemp after 2019; R1 keeps 2016 as its warmest year. The dashed line is R1 with fitted steps removed. Right: R1 global T2m minus ERA5, R1 land T2m minus GHCN-CAMS, and R1 ocean T2m minus COBE-SST2 (3-month means).

Top: change of R1 skin temperature minus COBE-SST2 at the 2020 break (left) and at the 2022-2023 breaks (right). Bottom left: R1 June-August land T2m minus GHCN-CAMS, 2020-2025 minus 2014-2019. Bottom right: R1 snow-covered fraction of land north of 30N; summer snow doubles from 2020 and winter snow nearly disappears in early 2023.
